version.x-source: MR-001 rejects an invalid semver; Decision Register section 5.5 specifies Semantic Versioning, so a prerelease and build metadata are valid and must not be rejected.

owner_role.x-source: Decision Register section 4.2 Registry assigns one owner role per module.

capability_key.x-source: Pattern is a DECLARED INFERENCE. MR-002 states no key syntax.

version.x-source: Integer major version. DECLARED INFERENCE, and in tension with Decision Register section 5.5 which specifies Semantic Versioning for contracts; whether a capability version follows semver is an owner decision and is unresolved.

capabilities.x-source: MR-002 requires deterministic resolution of a duplicate capability. Keying and versioning a capability is a DECLARED INFERENCE from that requirement; MR-002 does not state the shape.

dependencies.x-source: MR-003 blocks a circular, missing or incompatible dependency with a stable error.

permissions.x-source: MR-001 rejects a manifest missing its permission policy.

cost_policy.x-source: MR-001 rejects a manifest missing its cost policy.

classification.x-source: MR-001 rejects a manifest missing its data policy. The three classification VALUES are a DECLARED INFERENCE: `synthetic-only` and `permissioned-data` follow CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md, and `tenant-data` appears nowhere in docs/ and is this contract's own term.

data_policy.x-source: MR-001 rejects a manifest missing its data policy.

reason.x-source: MR-006 requires support to see the last error without seeing a secret. A stable key rather than free text is a DECLARED INFERENCE from CTR-ERR-001, which uses a Thai message key for user-facing text.

missing.x-source: MR-004 names exactly "missing secret/scope/entitlement". `permission` and `health` are DECLARED INFERENCES from MR-004 Inputs, which lists "secret handles, entitlement, health, permission". `dependency` was present in an earlier draft with no source and has been removed.

lifecycle.x-source: MR-005 names the four lifecycle hooks initialize / readiness / drain / shutdown, and MR-004 makes activation deny-by-default. The six state LABELS are a DECLARED INFERENCE: MR-005 names hooks, not states, and `registered`, `initializing`, `draining`, `stopped` and `blocked` appear nowhere in the workstream document. MR-004 does not mention a reason; requiring one is inferred from MR-006, which requires support to see the last error without seeing a secret.

secret_handles.x-source: PT-010 requires that a manifest sees a scoped REFERENCE only and that logs, events and jobs never contain a secret. The `secret:` token itself is a DECLARED INFERENCE - PT-010 gives "reference only" and names no syntax. See open_blockers: CTR-SEC-001 (owner A0+A1) is the chartered owner of handle syntax and this single-owner contract must not fix it.

then.x-rule: MR-004 deny-by-default: a module cannot be ready unless activation readiness explicitly succeeded.

MR-004: a blocked module must record what was missing, so support can act without seeing a secret (MR-006). An empty array satisfied the previous form; independent review showed "missing": [] was accepted while the rule read as closed.

allOf.x-rule: CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md: "A package using permissioned data must declare classification, consent, retention, and redaction." The schema previously required only classification and tenant_scoped, so permissioned-data with tenant_scoped false was accepted. Raised by independent security review.
